title: Fear-Avoidance Responses and Return-to-Sport Duration Following Injury in Elite Adolescent Field Hockey Players
abstract: Abstract: This study examined the association between fear-avoidance responses and return-to-sport duration across various injury types in elite adolescent field hockey players. I prospectively monitored elite adolescent athletes following injury, assessed their fear-avoidance using the Athletes’ Fear Avoidance Questionnaire (AFAQ), and recorded the return-to-sport duration. To account for the nested structure of repeated injuries within individual athletes, I used linear mixed-effects models, with injury type, AFAQ score, age, and sex as fixed effects and athlete identity as a random effect. The results showed significant variation across injury types, with ligament injuries associated with the highest fear-avoidance scores and longest return-to-sport duration. Higher fear-avoidance scores were significantly associated with longer return-to-sport duration after accounting for injury type, age, and sex. These findings suggest that fear-avoidance may be an important factor associated with return-to-sport duration, highlighting the potential value of addressing psychological responses during adolescent sports rehabilitation.

journal.name: Journal of Applied Sport and Exercise Psychology-Zeitschrift fur Sportpsychologie
